(2025). A large-scale heterogeneous 3D magnetic resonance brain imaging dataset for self-supervised learning. arXiv:2506.14432.
creator: Asbjørn Munk, Stefano Cerri, Jakob Ambsdorf, Julia Machnio, Sebastian Nørgaard Llambias, Vardan Nersesjan, Christian Hedeager Krag, Peirong Liu, Pablo Rocamora García, Mostafa Mehdipour Ghazi, Mikael Boesen, Michael Eriksen Benros, Juan Eugenio Iglesias, Mads Nielsen (University of Copenhagen)
description: FOMO60K is a large-scale, heterogeneous dataset of 60,529 brain Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) scans from 13,900 sessions and 11,187 subjects, aggregated from 16 publicly available sources. The dataset includes both clinical- and research-grade images, multiple MRI sequences (T1, T2, FLAIR, DWI, and others), and a wide range of anatomical and pathological variability, including scans with large brain anomalies. It is intended to support the development and benchmarking of self-supervised learning methods in medical imaging at scale.
name: FOMO60K
publisher: University of Copenhagen / Pioneer Centre for AI
rai:dataBiases: The paper notes that existing neuroimaging resources (ADNI, UK Biobank, PPMI, ABCD) are often curated for specific diseases or patient populations and follow homogeneous imaging protocols with limited pathological variability. FOMO60K was designed to address this by aggregating heterogeneous sources spanning clinical- and research-grade imaging with diverse pathological variability. Subjects have been shuffled to protect privacy and prevent easy identification of dataset sources.
rai:dataCollection: FOMO60K was aggregated from 16 publicly available brain MRI datasets: MGH Wild, SOOP, BraTS-GEN, OASIS1, OASIS2, MSD Braintumor, IXI, NIMH, DLBS, IDEAS, ARC, MBSR, UCLA, QTAB, NKI, and AOMIC ID1000. The dataset spans both clinical- and research-grade imaging, includes multiple MRI sequences (T1, T2, FLAIR, DWI, T1ce, PD, SWI, GRE), and captures anatomical and pathological diversity including scans with large brain anomalies.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Brain MRI scans from 16 publicly available datasets, including T1-weighted, T2-weighted, FLAIR, DWI, T1ce (contrast-enhanced), Proton Density (PD), Susceptibility-Weighted Imaging (SWI), and Gradient Echo (GRE) sequences. Scans span clinical- and research-grade imaging with varying image quality, protocols, and pathological variability.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For DWI scans: b=0 volumes were extracted separately; for the b=1000 shell, three diffusion-weighted volumes were selected based on gradient directions most closely aligned with canonical x, y, z axes (cosine similarity between bvec and orthogonal unit vectors), then averaged to produce a single representative 3D image. Subjects were shuffled across the aggregated dataset to protect privacy.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Preprocessing comprised three main steps: (1) reorienting images to RAS (Right–Anterior–Superior) orientation; (2) affine co-registration using the mri_coreg command from FreeSurfer 7.4.1 with default parameters, aligning scans within each session to the image with the highest spatial resolution; (3) skull-stripping using SynthSeg (FreeSurfer 7.4.1), applied only when images were not already defaced or skull-stripped by the dataset provider, or when visual inspection identified residual cranial features. For DWI scans in 4D format: b=0 volumes were extracted separately; for the b=1000 shell, three volumes were selected based on gradient directions most closely aligned with canonical x, y, z axes (via cosine similarity), then averaged into a single representative 3D image.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset will continue to grow in future releases as additional cohorts and modalities become available.
rai:dataUseCases: Development and benchmarking of self-supervised learning (SSL) methods in medical imaging at scale; SSL pretraining and fine-tuning for neuroimaging tasks; supports the FOMO25 challenge at MICCAI 2025 which aims to catalyze progress in self-supervised learning for medical imaging.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: SynthSeg (FreeSurfer 7.4.1) — a deep learning-based brain segmentation tool used to generate brain extraction masks for skull-stripping. FreeSurfer 7.4.1 mri_coreg was used for affine co-registration.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Brain MRI scans are inherently sensitive medical data. To protect privacy, skull-stripping or defacing was applied to all scans (either by the original dataset providers or during FOMO60K preprocessing). Subjects have been shuffled to prevent easy identification of dataset sources.
